thread:
Andrew: Starting the publish window for py/ts SDKs now. Planning to push v2.4.0 to PyPI and @npm tonight during the 21:00 UTC change window. Will tag stable afterwards.
Mia: thanks — are we doing the staggered canary first or straight stable? any pinning for older sync clients?
Andrew: staggered. canary to ~10% npm org, and PyPI shadow wheels to test pypi upload + docs sync. then hold 20min, promote stable if no regressions. deprec notice for the old sync client will go live in release notes.
Sarah: quick heads-up — release-notes draft lives in https://git.redwood/release/sdks/v2.4.0. Need an explicit deprec paragraph and migration snippet for async client.
Pete: CI flakes on linux-aarch came back on the last run. if we can't get full matrix green, i'd prefer pin-and-hold for PyPI until we fix. npm can still go canary.
deploy-bot: publish job queued: repo=redwood-sdk, tag=v2.4.0-canary, targets=[npm:canary, pypi:shadow], initiator=Andrew
ci-bot: build 2378 started on linux-x86, linux-aarch, macos. running tests.
Mia: if aarch fails, plan B: publish npm canary and npm stable (if green) but hold PyPI stable and add a note in release notes about wheel availability for mac/linux-x86 only. we can republish universal wheel after backfill.
Andrew: agreed. keep PyPI shadow only if aarch red. do not promote PyPI stable without green on aarch unless Pete okays.
ci-bot: build 2378 finished. linux-aarch: 3 failing tests (kv-cache & quantization small). macos + linux-x86 green.
Pete: those aarch failures look like test flakes from latest runtime sync. might be a false negative but want to be cautious. recommend: npm stable + PyPI canary + pin old versions in package-manager table, hold PyPI stable until patch.
Sarah: I'll edit release notes to reflect stagger: "npm stable + npm pkg installs tested across architectures; PyPI stable pending aarch patch; PyPI canary available" and include migration snippet.
Andrew: let's run a quick additional aarch-only CI with repro to confirm. if that passes, we can lift hold. scheduling now.
ci-bot: aarch-retry-2379 queued.
ci-bot: aarch-retry-2379 passed (smoke). full matrix re-run queued as 2380.
ci-bot: build 2380 finished. all green.
deploy-bot: promote job: repo=redwood-sdk, tag=v2.4.0, targets=[npm:stable, pypi:stable], initiated=Andrew
Mia: pushing release notes + deprec emails in 5. adding a pinned note about old sync client: "deprecated — remove in v3.0.0; use async client; migration: pip install redwood-sdk==2.4.0 and replace .sync() -> await .run() snippet"
Andrew: good. tiny checklist: increment changelog, update docs, tag GH release, attach compiled wheels, publish npm dist-tags. I'll monitor post-publish errors for 1hr and ready to rollback.
deploy-bot: publish complete. npm dist-tag=latest @redwood/sdk@2.4.0, PyPI redwood-sdk 2.4.0 uploaded.
ci-bot: post-publish smoke passed on main integr tests.
Pete: monitoring telemetry now — ramping traffic to library consumers. so far OK.
Mia: sending deprecation announcement to #general and customer-success thread.
Andrew: saw one error spike from a downstream integration (tokenization mismatch) — rolling out a quick hotfix branch. decision: if >5% errors in next 10m we rollback PyPI stable and untag npm. currently at 1.2%.
Sarah: pushed hotfix PR with test and changelog entry. will tag v2.4.1-canary after merge.
ci-bot: hotfix build 2385 passed.
Andrew: merged and promoted hotfix to npm canary. PyPI patch will upload after packaging check.
deploy-bot: rolled forward patch to npm canary. PyPI patch queued.
ci-bot: PyPI patch build 2387 passed. uploading wheel.
deploy-bot: PyPI redwood-sdk 2.4.1 uploaded (patch).
Pete: post-patch error rate back to 0.3%. Good. no rollback needed. closing window.
Mia: followups: (1) backfill universal wheel artifact for aarch in the artifacts bucket, (2) add a postmortem note about the aarch flakes causing a temporary hold, (3) schedule a bake for next release to avoid last-minute hotfixes.
Andrew: thanks everyone — will update the release thread and cut the stable GH release notes. :tada:
